title: NASA Announces the X-70, a New Experimental Aircraft
paragraphs: NASA has announced the X-70 Fractal, a new experimental aircraft, at an event at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on 4 November. It is a crewed research plane that the agency describes as highly adaptable and designed to speed up the testing of new aviation technology.

According to NASA, the X-70 can carry up to 2,000 pounds of experimental equipment, inside and outside the plane, and the equipment can be swapped quickly. It has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds, cruises at Mach 0.75, can reach 45,000 feet and has a range of about 1,500 nautical miles. Scientists plan to test flight-control and manoeuvring technologies.

However, the plane has not flown yet. NASA leader Jared Isaacman said the first flight under the NASA name should happen within the next two years, which is an expectation, not a fixed date. The agency's pictures are computer-generated, and NASA has not shared who builds the plane or how much it costs.

questions.q: What will the X-70 be used for?
questions.a: To test new flight-control and manoeuvring technologies.

questions.q: What are two of its performance numbers?
questions.a: Cruise speed of Mach 0.75 and a maximum height of 45,000 feet.

questions.q: What information has NASA not shared?
questions.a: Who builds the plane and how much it costs.
